history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration expedite the audits of implementing partners and financial closure processes of projects to ensure timely refunds and project closure, with a view to improving the efficient utilization of funds thereof.
history.administration_response: The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has ensured that audits are conducted, where operational context allows, within the nine-month time frame provided for in the global guidelines for country-based pooled funds. Furthermore, with the existence of the new audit-related long-term agreements, which have been available since December 2024, we expect a shorter lead time for audit completion and financial closure. We therefore consider this recommendation to be implemented and request that it be closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the delay in external audit and financial closing procedures has persisted during the audit of the 2024 financial year, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration expedite the audits of implementing partners and financial closure processes of projects to ensure timely refunds and project closure with a view to improving the efficient utilization of funds thereof.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. A total of 985 projects funded under the allocations for 2024 and prior years are currently undergoing audit within the humanitarian financing units, with varying timelines, in line with the newly established general audit long- term agreements. The completion of audits is an ongoing process and is linked to each project’s end date. The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs will continue to conduct internal follow-ups to ensure the timely completion of audits within nine months of project closure.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs will continue to conduct internal follow-ups to ensure the timely completion of audits, and based on the information from the One Grant Management System, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
